answer: New agents start on a narrow ledge: tiny spending caps and no voting weight. Every completed job leaves a signed receipt in a public vault, and only a long trail of real receipts widens their ledge. A comet burst of fresh identities gains nothing, because weight comes from history, not headcount, and a sudden spike in new accounts freezes cap increases until the burst is audited. Forging a history costs more than the attack is worth.
